It is April 17, 2026 now. On my land, the wheat is already in the field, cotton is the one I need to plant now, and maize will go in right after wheat harvest in June. I only have 9 mu, so I will keep the usual way: 6 mu in wheat-maize double cropping, and 3 mu in cotton. I do not like changing too much. Last year this way at least kept grain in hand and some cash from cotton. Neighbors around me do about the same. I have well water, but pumping costs money, so I only irrigate at the key times. Fertilizer also cannot be too light. If I save too much and the crop turns weak, then the loss is bigger than the money saved. But I also cannot throw money around, because family spending is heavy with 7 people in the house. So this year I will do a steady plan, not the highest input, not the lowest either.

For wheat, I already have it on 6 mu, planted last October. I will give one more topdressing and 2 irrigations if the weather stays dry, mainly at jointing and filling. I want the wheat to finish well, because if wheat is poor, the maize after it also gets rushed. After harvest in early June, I will plant summer maize on the same 6 mu quickly, within a few days, with hybrid seed like most people here. The turnaround is tight, so I will use simple tillage and fast sowing, not spend too much time making the field pretty. For cotton, I will plant 3 mu around late April. Cotton brings cash if the year is decent, but it takes more watching and more hand work, so I only keep a smaller area. I will fertilize it moderately and irrigate only if it really turns dry.
